# [Perf] muse-spark: Overlap non-NVFP4 pre-expert norm with routing

[Upstream PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47985) · state: open · merged: False

## Original PR description

## Outstanding validation

- **TRT-LLM BF16:** real-backend correctness, CUDA graph capture/replay, and A/B performance remain unvalidated on SM10x. The B200 attempt stopped during image extraction before tests started.
- **Performance:** RTX 5090 Triton measurements below use a reduced 16-expert configuration. Full-model / serving A/B and representative profiles remain outstanding; the observed component-level changes do not establish a serving speedup.
- GPU CI must run separately; the previous draft-gated skipped jobs are not passes. Native INT4/AMX execution is also untested.

## Motivation

Muse Spark's non-NVFP4, non-SP pre-expert RMSNorm reads the main-stream pooler output independently of routing. Enqueue it before the router join to overlap those operations.

## Modifications

- Move only this norm ahead of the existing router join. Preserve NVFP4 fused norm/quant ownership, SP normalization, stream waits and eager `record_stream` calls.
- Add a small real `MuseSpark1xMoE` regression using the production weighted norms, pooler dispatcher, router/routing and BF16 expert backend. Register the small-GPU path on `1-gpu-small`; the TRT-LLM case requires a separate SM10x run.
- Add a real-backend paired A/B driver. Retain the earlier dependency-light scheduling tests and add the CPU-only INT4 selection/order check.

## Validation

The production scheduling change is the same as `366538a2b52bbc8ca49c4fbe214b857d9d4be227`; the baseline host method is extracted from `efdcb420c75e7014bc9148b085a8fcdd3154e7e1` and executed with the same production operator implementations and weights as the candidate.

### CPU / INT4 scope

Three local host tests pass: branch/stream ordering, CPU numerical/empty-input cases, and INT4 CPU-only selection plus serial call order. `_uses_gptq_int4_experts` selects GPTQ/AutoRound GPTQ experts only on CPU. This change does not introduce CUDA overlap for that path. These are scope/order checks, not execution of the native GPTQ/AMX expert kernels.

### Real BF16 components

Random weights, TP=EP=1; no model checkpoint download. The correctness fixture constructs the actual `MuseSpark1xMoE`, including weighted zero-centered-gamma pre-norm with config epsilon `1e-5`, weighted input-scale post-norm with epsilon `1e-8`, FP32 router and production routing. Dimensions: hidden 1024 / expert hidden 512 / intermediate 512 / 16 experts / top-k 8 (hidden 512 when no projection).

Each tested backend covers projection on/off and tokens 1, 16, 128, 129. After warmup, eager outputs and five changing-input CUDA graph replays per case must match serialized execution exactly (`rtol=atol=0`).

**rtx5090:** `{"python": "3.12.16", "torch": "2.14.1+cu130", "cuda": "13.0", "gpu": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090", "capability": [12, 0], "tf32": false}`

### Pending TRT-LLM validation

The SM10x B200 attempt was stopped during container image extraction, before tests started. TRT-LLM correctness, capture/replay and A/B remain unvalidated. This coverage remains pending and should be considered before merging. INT4 validation above is limited to CPU selection/order; native AMX execution remains untested.

### A/B protocol and interpretation

Actual production BF16 expert kernels, hidden 8192 / expert hidden 4096 / intermediate 4096 / **16 experts** / top-k 8. The expert count is reduced to fit small single-GPU validation and is not the full 256-expert model. Two seeds, eager and graph modes, 20 alternating-order pairs of 50 iterations for each token count. Same weights/inputs/backend within each pair; graph runs also validate changing-input replay against serialized execution. CUDA events measure the caller stream including the router join. TF32 is off; clocks are not locked. Triton uses its default configuration where no matching tuned file exists.

RTX 5090 graph differences were approximately -0.06% to +0.79%; eager -0.08% to +0.42%. The unchanged-code graph control ranged from -0.081% to +0.044%, which is a noise diagnostic rather than a confidence interval. The small-token improvements are modest; larger-token results are near neutral. Do not extrapolate these measurements to serving throughput or latency.

The earlier H200 surrogate fixture passed eager/graph/allocator tests and Compute Sanitizer memcheck (0 errors). Its graph improvement (11.5–19.1%) used replacement torch operators and **does not represent real-backend performance**. The real-backend results above supersede it for performance interpretation.

Full-model accuracy, serving A/B, distributed TP/EP/SP and real NVFP4 kernels are not validated here. The small single-rank test does not establish those results. Upstream GPU CI status must be assessed separately; skipped or maintainer-gated checks are not passes.

### Reproduce

```bash
git show efdcb420c75e7014bc9148b085a8fcdd3154e7e1:python/sglang/srt/models/muse_spark.py > /tmp/muse_base.py
python test/manual/muse_spark/test_norm_overlap.py TestHostSchedule -v
python test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_muse_spark_norm_overlap.py -v
# Run each backend on supported hardware; --graph is optional for eager A/B.
python test/manual/muse_spark/bench_real_norm_overlap.py --baseline-source /tmp/muse_base.py --backend triton --experts 16 --tokens 1 16 128 129 --seed 0 --pairs 20 --iterations 50 --graph
```
